title: FLIGENT-Net: A Fourier-Linearized Graph Network with Vision Transformer in Gastric Histopathology Image Classification
content: Gastric cancer is one of the leading causes of oncological mortality worldwide and is frequently diagnosed at advanced stages due to non-specific early symptoms. Manual histopathological analysis remains the gold standard but is exhaustive, subjective, and prone to inter-observer variability. Current deep learning models for gastric cancer detection are predominantly limited to local spatial analysis via convolutions, often discarding ambiguous tissue patches during preprocessing to inflate performance metrics, thereby ignoring subtle spectral textures critical for early-stage diagnosis. This paper presents FLIGENT-Net, a hybrid multi-domain architecture designed for adenocarcinoma detection on the GasHisSDB dataset without patch exclusion. The proposed framework integrates a novel FLI-Extractor module that concurrently combines morphological feature extraction through convolutional neural networks with spectral texture analysis via Fast Fourier Transform. These multi-domain features are processed through dynamic topological routing using graph neural networks and global context modeling via a Vision Transformer. Ablation studies and systematic hyperparameter calibration (τ = 0.70, class_threshold = 0.55) demonstrate that the optimal configuration achieves a sensitivity of 89.50% and an F1-score of 81.80%. Although the global accuracy is lower than that of pure spatial ensemble models exceeding 99%, which systematically discard up to 44.23% of normal patches, FLIGENT-Net prioritizes false negative reduction over global accuracy. This design establishes a clinically superior trade-off for oncological screening, where missing a malignant case carries catastrophic consequences compared to manageable false alarms.
